conceptual assets.information: The compressed instruction and its reconstructed 32-bit operation, including opcode, operands, immediates and function fields, on which the CPU depends for correct execution.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The instruction may contain proprietary code, and its decoded operation is exposed through instr_o at lines 299-301 after processing instr_i at lines 57-58 and 72-76. Changing instr_i or the decode assignments changes opcode, operands or immediates in instr_o, for example at lines 72-76 and 299-301.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe the decoded output to recover proprietary instruction behavior or alter instr_i so that the CPU executes a different operation.

conceptual assets.information: The internally generated decision that classifies an input encoding as illegal and controls whether bit 1 of the decoded instruction is passed. It has no direct entry or exit port because it is derived by tests of instr_i and only controls instr_o.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Corrupting the illegal decision or its deciding conditions can accept an illegal encoding or alter a legal decoded instruction, and the decision directly controls instr_o(1) at line 300. Because the decision gates instr_o(1), forcing it high can withhold that required output bit and disrupt instruction delivery at line 300.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could corrupt the illegal-detection logic or its inputs so illegal instructions are accepted or decoded instructions are suppressed, disrupting correct execution.
